reason: This passage (Judges 9) contains no instances of Yahweh directly complaining about or expressing verbal displeasure with the people. While God does take punitive action—sending an evil spirit between Abimelech and the men of Shechem, and returning their wickedness upon their own heads—these are acts of judgment rather than expressions of complaint. The only speeches recorded are from Abimelech, Jotham (in his parable), and various human characters. No divine complaint or lamentation is narrated or quoted in this text.
